### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class), loadMany (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `12d398b162dc37acfae6c43f2112e620d4327494` — the merge of head `a43fc250331266aaf1e9291de90dfeede2136870` into base `d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 12d398b162dc37acfae6c43f2112e620d4327494 && git checkout 12d398b162dc37acfae6c43f2112e620d4327494
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2 a43fc250331266aaf1e9291de90dfeede2136870 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2 && git merge --no-ff a43fc250331266aaf1e9291de90dfeede2136870

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `426f47c9a9c3c0e55f307b1def9075e3c804b514`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Face: declaration. The diff touches `.changeset/32986-host-unregister-keeps-environment-rows.md`, `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts` and `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts`. None is a published schema or a governed path. The changeset says `Clause-②: no — …`, which is not `no (narrowing)`, so there is no ④. I judged the tree at the head, read against `main` and against `@objectstack/metadata@18.3.0` (`83d7e4ae`).

**Mechanism, as read.** For a type outside `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`, `loadMany` now adds every item that a `datasource:` loader handed on with no package (`indexedItemPackageId(item) === undefined`) to `storedEnvironmentRows`. That is a WeakSet, keyed on object identity. `DatabaseLoader.handOut` gives the boot pass a fresh copy. `applyProtection` stamps that same object in place, and `register` → `writeRegistryEntry` stores that same object. So the mark reaches the registry entry. `unregisterPackage` skips a non-slotted item when it is marked, its `_packageId` names the package, and neither its own `packageId` nor its `package` does. Nothing else reads the set. The slotted branch (`storedPackagelessRows`) keeps exactly what it did before, so no other caller's answer changes.

**Each class, held up against the tree:**
- *Every type the card names* (`object`, `view`, `app`, `hook`, `dashboard`): kept, in the registry and in storage. The first pin seeds one package-less row of each type, runs the real `_loadFromFileSystem`, and checks that the stamp is still there before the removal and that all five survive it. Every other non-slotted type gets the same rule but has no pin, as the PR body says.
- *The host's own stored row* (body carries `_packageId: HOST`, as `register` seeds a stamped file or artifact item): `indexedItemPackageId` is defined, so the row is not marked and is removed. Pinned by CONTROL 2.
- *Host item from code or files:* it never passes a `datasource:` loader, so it is not marked and is removed. The pin covers the code case (`registerInMemory`). The file case follows by reading, because a file loader is not `datasource:`.
- *Package-less row the boot pass files under the host (cf. #32791 / PR #32802):* for these types the pass registers with `skipSourceLoader`, so the stamp is never written back into the source row. `bindReadRowPackage` acts only on slotted legacy rows. The next boot reads the row package-less again and marks it again.
- *Package's override of an environment item, and the `.custom` pair:* a non-slotted row that names its package in its body (`packageId` / `_packageId`) is not marked. It stays a member of its own package and of no other. A package-less environment edit of a host item is kept after `unregisterPackage(HOST)`. That already happens on `main`, because a protocol write registers an unstamped new object, so it is not moved here. It matches 18.3.0.
- *Drafts versus active:* `readTypeRows` does not filter on `state`, and the mark ignores state, so a `draft` row is treated like an `active` one. No pin covers it (nit below).
- *Legacy `package: HOST` body:* `storedItemPackageId` does not read `package`, so the row is marked and stamped. The `meta.package !== packageId` clause keeps it a member, so it is removed, as in 18.3.0. The clause is live but no test pins it (should-fix S2).
- *Row whose `package_id` column names HOST but whose body names no package:* for a non-slotted type, `readTypeRows` ignores the column, so the row is marked and kept. That matches 18.3.0. No first-party writer of a non-slotted row sets the column (`save` writes `binding` only for a slot).

**Where the fix stops (S1).** The mark lives on the registry object, not on the stored row. Any later write that replaces the object with a copy that keeps `_packageId: HOST` drops the mark. That write also persists the stamp into the environment row's stored body through `DatabaseLoader.save`, and from then on the row reads as the host's own, in this process and after a restart. Two such writes are on the head, both outside this diff:
- ObjectQL's late-manifest bridge (`bridgeManifestObjectsToMetadataService`, enabled unconditionally at `plugin.ts` L1681). When another package extends an environment object that ObjectQL owns as `HOST`, the `ownPreviousCopy` arm re-`register`s the merged object with `_packageId: HOST`. Its withdrawal counterpart, `restoreExtendedObjectCopies`, does the same.
- `publishPackage` / `revertPackage`. They build `{ ...item.data, … }` over `collectPackageMembers`, which still includes stamped environment rows, and `register` the result.

After either write, `unregisterPackage(HOST)` deletes the environment row again. That is the data loss this card is about. Neither write is a regression from this PR, since both persist the stamp on `main` and in 18.3.0. But #32198 is what turns them into deletion, and this PR's mark cannot see them.

**Tests under ablation (judged by reading):**
- Delete the guard line: pins 1 and 3 fail, as the body measured.
- Delete the `else storedEnvironmentRows.add`: the same two fail.
- Drop the `storedEnvironmentRows.has` test: CONTROL 2 (stamped body) and pin 3 (`host_thing`) fail.
- `!slotted &&` is redundant, because the set holds no slotted item. Its ablation changes nothing, and it is harmless.
- Delete `meta.package !== packageId`: no test fails (S2).
- `meta._packageId === packageId` set to `true`: no test fails. It only skips non-members, so it is harmless.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata` **patch**: correct. The change fixes behaviour #32198 introduced and has not shipped, and adds no surface: the new set and method are `private`.
- The changeset text matches the diff. The rule applies to every non-slotted type. The host's own stamped-body rows and in-memory and file items are removed as before. Types stored per `(package, name)` are untouched. The ObjectQL owner (`_packageId ?? 'metadata-service'`) does not move, because the stamp is untouched.
- The sentence "leaves the environment's own rows as the released version does" holds for rows still marked. Per S1 it does not hold for rows a bridge or publish has rewritten. Stating that limit is part of S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Clause-②: no` confirmed.** In 18.3.0, `unregisterPackage` selected by `meta?.packageId === packageName || meta?.package === packageName`. The new guard skips only items where neither key names the package. So nothing 18.3.0 removed is kept now, and no released answer narrows. On `main` the PR does narrow the removal, but only of #32198's unreleased widening. The face stays declaration.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` confirmed.** No `packages/metadata-protocol` file is touched and no protocol read moves.
- **Order after #32812.** The dependency is the claim's file surface, not correctness. #32812 changes the slotted stamp. This PR is gated on `!slotted` and its mark sits in the `else` arm. If this PR lands first, nothing breaks. #32812 would at most get a textual conflict in `loadMany`'s three-line mark block. #32812 has no PR, and this card is owed before the release that ships #32198 (owed item 3). So holding this PR behind #32812 is a schedule risk, not a safety need (nit N3).
- **Check-runs on the head:**
  - `PR-body guards` = **failure**. Its annotation reads "closes #32986 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/project-thread-im2gsb`". The card's restated claim (third comment, `Restates: 6841685641`) does name that branch, so the run most likely predates the restatement, and a re-run should clear it. Not a contract finding, but the PR is not merge-ready until it is green.
  - In progress: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–8, three Type Check jobs, and two Lint jobs. The new pins have not yet run in CI at this head.
  - `Check Changeset`, `ESLint`, `query-options erasure`, `PM dispatch-gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` passed.

Findings:
- **should-fix S1:** the mark rides object identity. The ObjectQL late-manifest bridge (`ownPreviousCopy` re-register, and `restoreExtendedObjectCopies`) and `publishPackage` / `revertPackage` replace a marked environment row with a copy that keeps `_packageId: HOST`, and persist that stamp into its stored body. After that, `unregisterPackage(HOST)` deletes the row again, in this process or after a restart. File a card that gates the release shipping #32198, and state the limit in the PR body and changeset instead of "every type … is kept".
- **should-fix S2:** add a pin for a package-less stored row whose body names HOST through the legacy `package` key. It must still be removed. That clause is what keeps 18.3.0's answer, and today it can be deleted without any test going red.
- **nit N1:** no pin for a `state: 'draft'` environment row. It behaves like `active` by reading.
- **nit N2:** the non-slotted types beyond the card's five (for example `flow`, `page`, `report`) are covered by the rule but not pinned.
- **nit N3:** the "lands after #32812" order is file-surface only. Landing first is safe, and the lane should not hold a p1 data-loss fix behind a card with no PR.

No must-fix.

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a43fc250331266aaf1e9291de90dfeede2136870`

### ① Derived judgments

This is a delta review over my PASS on `426f47c9`, on the declaration face. The changeset still reads `Clause-②: no — …`, not `no (narrowing)`, so there is still no ④.

**What changed.** The compare from `426f47c9` to `a43fc250` is `ahead` 1, `behind` 0: one commit, `a43fc250`, whose parent is `426f47c9`. There is no rebase and no merge of `main`, so the compare is the net delta. It touches two files:
- `.changeset/32986-host-unregister-keeps-environment-rows.md` (+4 −2);
- `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts` (+13).

`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts` is unchanged, so every judgment from the earlier record on the mechanism, the classes and the ablations stands. Nothing else moved.

**S1, the stated limit: resolved.**
- **PR body.** The new paragraph "The limit (triage should-fix S1)" says a row is kept only while the boot pass's mark is still on it. It names both writes:
  - the late-manifest bridge's `ownPreviousCopy` re-register and `restoreExtendedObjectCopies`;
  - `publishPackage` / `revertPackage` of the host.

  It also says the write persists the stamp through `DatabaseLoader.save`, which re-arms the deletion in-process and after a restart. That matches what I read on the tree. The readers bullet in the Acceptance notes now separates the boot bridge (skips) from the late-manifest bridge (replaces). That is accurate.
- **Changeset.** The new "The limit" paragraph names "ObjectQL's late-manifest bridge, `publishPackage` and `revertPackage` of the host". It does not name the withdrawal restore separately. The bridge's restore is part of the same bridge, so the statement is not wrong, only less specific than the PR body (nit N1). The `Clause-②` sentence is narrowed to "the environment's own rows the boot pass marked", which is accurate.
- **#33003** is open, `priority:p1`, `pm:dispatched`, `domain:server`, and claimed by `epic:#31527#2`. Its "What happens" carries both writes with the same detail: the `ownPreviousCopy` arm and `restoreExtendedObjectCopies`, and `publishPackage` / `revertPackage` over `collectPackageMembers`. Its "Do" also asks for:
  - a route that survives a rewrite;
  - per-write keep pins in-process and after a reboot, with CONTROLs and ablations;
  - the earlier nits N1 (draft row) and N2 (a non-slotted type beyond the five);
  - a `Clause-②` declaration.

  It is gated on the release that ships #32198 and ordered after PR #32999.

**S2, the legacy-key pin: resolved. Red under ablation, by reading.** The new CONTROL seeds each of the five types package-less, with body `{ name, label: 'env', package: HOST }`.
- `storedItemPackageId` reads only the envelope's `packageId` and the body's `_packageId` (`package-slotted-store.ts`, `peelStoredEnvelope`), never `package`. So `loadMany` adds each row to `storedEnvironmentRows`.
- `applyProtection` writes `_packageId` whenever it is unset (`protection.zod.ts`), so each row is stamped `HOST`. The pin's pre-removal assertion `[type, HOST, 'env', 1]` checks exactly that.
- With `meta.package !== packageId` in place, `isStampedEnvironmentRow` is false. `isPackageMember` holds, and `unregisterAt` deletes the non-slotted row by name. Expected after: `[type, null, null, 0]`.
- With that clause deleted, the guard returns true (marked, stamped `HOST`, no own `packageId`), so all five are skipped and stay `[type, HOST, 'env', 1]`. The after-removal assertion goes red for every type.
- The other two clauses cannot rescue it: `packageId` is undefined, and `_packageId === HOST` is true. The pin binds the clause that keeps 18.3.0's answer.

The earlier nit N3 (order after #32812) is answered too: the body now says the overlap is file surface only and the seat released the order.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata` **patch**: unchanged and correct. The delta adds prose and one test, and no surface. The changeset text still matches the diff, including the added "or names it under the legacy `package` key" among the host's own items.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand. Code is unchanged since the earlier confirmation against `@objectstack/metadata@18.3.0`.
- **Check-runs on `a43fc250`:**
  - `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`: **success**, on both runs. The earlier failure has cleared.
  - Success: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, every `Lint ·` job, `Lint & Repo Gates`, all four `Type Check ·` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`, and `Test Core` 4/8, 5/8 and 6/8.
  - Still in progress: `Test Core` 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 7/8 and 8/8. CI has not yet shown the five `[#32986]` cases green at this head. The PR body reports `database-loader.test.ts` 276 passed (276) locally on `a43fc250`. Merge waits on the remaining shards.

Findings:
- **nit N1:** the changeset's limit names "ObjectQL's late-manifest bridge" but not its withdrawal restore (`restoreExtendedObjectCopies`), which the PR body and #33003 both name. It is not wrong, only less specific.

No must-fix. No should-fix open: S1 and S2 are resolved. The earlier N1 and N2 are carried by #33003, and N3 is answered in the body.
